discoveries:
- `/tmp/w2-154-eng` (the brief's TMPDIR) is read-only in this sandbox, so I used `$TMPDIR/w2-154-eng` instead, as EMG-d4b allows.
- Writes under `.gov-runtime/scratch/` were denied partway through (one Write and one compound `sed`). I moved my scratch scripts to `$TMPDIR` and did not retry those calls.
- **Slip, already undone:** my first plugin trial script ran `cd` into a folder that did not exist. It wrote a test `conftest.py` over `tests/conftest.py` in the worktree and added four stray `tests/test_*.py` files. I restored the conftest with `git checkout HEAD -- tests/conftest.py` and deleted the four files, which I created. `git status` was clean afterwards, and the conftest never reached a commit.
- The repo's conftest reports opted-out cases as deselected, so `pytest_deselected` is a reliable signal. A case named by node id on the command line is run even if opted out, so only whole-file or whole-folder entries become "not in this run".

risks:
- Any deselection counts, not only the opt-in lists. A `-k` or `-m` filter that removes an entry's every case would also make it "not in this run" instead of exit 4. The Interface says "other plugins", so I kept it.
- The nightly's serial run does not switch the opt-in lists on, so an entry the lists leave out gives N of 0 there. With only such entries, I3 reads that as `verdict: red serial: 0 cases run`. That follows the ticket's wording, but S4's restored `ui_off` entry will be a case-less nightly serial run unless another entry runs too.
- `"not_in_this_run"` is always present (as a list, empty when nothing is out) on the serial-afterwards record. No existing test objected.
- The stub seam sets `HEAD` to `stub` and leaves the clone in place. The green-night clone removal only matches the real path pattern, so it prints "clone NOT removed: unexpected path".
- `bash -n` passes and the acceptance cases drive the stub. I did not run a real nightly.

lessons: a scratch script that `cd`s into a folder it just made must stop if the `cd` fails (`cd … || exit`). I used a `$TMPDIR`-relative path that did not exist and wrote into the worktree.
